name: Judo (British Judo Association)
description: The BJA grading schemes: Sho awards (ages 5 to 7), Mon grades (juniors), Kyu grades (adults) and Dan grades (black belts and above). Includes the Mon and Kyu syllabus checklists.

Combination: Kouchi-gari into Morote-seoi-nage
Combination: Ippon-seoi-nage into Kouchi-gari
Combination: Any technique with Seoi-otoshi or Kouchi-gari
Counter: Ouchi-gari countered by Tsuri-komi-goshi
Counter: Tai-otoshi countered by Kosoto-gari or Kosoto-gake
Ne-waza: Escape from Kesa-gatame using a bridge and roll

Ne-waza: Turnover from underneath Uke into Tate-shiho-gatame
Randori: Light randori with a cooperative partner for about three minutes
Two tachi-waza and one ne-waza technique, shown as a combination, a counter and a transition into ne-waza
Name three items from the judo moral code
Give two examples of actions (not grips) against the contest rules for negative or safety reasons
Demonstrate the proper procedure for entering and leaving the mat for a contest
Explain the meaning of: Shido, Hansoku-make
Demonstrate the referee's signals for Mate, Osaekomi, Toketa and adjusting the judogi
Explain the Japanese terminology for this grade
items.description: Kosoto-gake (Minor outer hook throw); Kosoto-gari (Minor outer reaping throw); Kouchi-gari (Minor inner reaping throw); Morote-seoi-nage (Two-handed shoulder throw); Ogoshi (Major hip throw); Osoto-gari (Major outer reaping throw); Seoi-otoshi (Shoulder drop throw); Tai-otoshi (Body drop throw); Tsuri-komi-goshi (Drawing hip throw); Yoko-shiho-gatame (Side four quarters hold)
